Alex.confusing: Round 3 egg counts: Drew's -2 and Casey's +0 at 7 cards. It was unclear how a Floofer hug and confusion could produce a loss with no Farm role that takes eggs.
Alex.fun: Round 2: my Kookaburra check on Blair matched her Tit claim, and the table converged on Casey. The Farm win and the 16 points were the high point.
Alex.change: Give players a bit more verifiable information. Unverifiable claims, like four people all saying they visited Ellis, made round 3 close to a coin flip.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I accepted the pile-on on Finley without questioning it. Finley's Eagle story did conflict with four claimed visits, but Ellis, the common target, was the Floofer. Hugging would explain Finley's zero eggs, so I should have suspected Ellis.

Blair.confusing: How Floofer hugging works. I couldn't tell who caused Drew's -2 in round 3, or how a hug related to it.
Blair.fun: Round 2, where the Eagle, Hawk and Tit reports all lined up on Casey. We caught the Meowfia and I banked 36 points in one throw.
Blair.change: Give clearer public information about which night effects can remove eggs. Round 3's -2 on Drew was a puzzle with no clean way to solve it.
Blair.regret: In round 3 I threw all four cards at Finley on a bandwagon. I should have noticed that Ellis, the leader, was the only person I had no real verification on, and that the claimed visits to her were mostly unverifiable. I should have kept a few cards and questioned the claims more.

Casey.confusing: How the vote tie-break and the consolation return interact with Meowfia not knowing each other. I also never worked out why Drew was at -2 in round 3, since no role I know of takes eggs.
Casey.fun: Round 3: my Owl claim and the push on Finley worked, and the table agreed on Finley within a couple of beats. I also liked seeing Ellis, my unknown teammate, push the same target.
Casey.change: Give Meowfia some way to find each other, or a clue about whether there are one or two of them. Without that, a Meowfia player ends up guessing blind.
Casey.regret: In round 2 I claimed Kookaburra after learning Ellis was Hawk. That clashed with Alex's real Kookaburra claim and got me eggsecuted. I should have claimed a role nobody could check, such as Turkey or Tit, or kept my claim vague.

Drew.confusing: The confused Kookaburra report in round 3: I couldn't tell whether the -2 was real or false, and I got no role info, so I didn't know how much to trust it.
Drew.fun: Round 2, when my Eagle report confirmed Ellis and Blair and the table piled onto Casey. Banking 35 points from one winning throw felt great.
Drew.change: I'd show the Kookaburra's confusion more clearly, or give the confused player some usable information. I'd also let players see who visited whom in round 1, so early lies are easier to catch.
Drew.regret: In round 3 I joined the pile on Finley without thinking. Ellis was the Floofer and had hugged me, which explains the confusion, and Finley's Eagle claim fit that. I should have questioned why four people all claimed to visit Ellis, and thrown less.

Ellis.confusing: How hugs and confusion produced the round 3 reports: Drew's -2 and Finley's Eagle result were hard to square with the visit claims, and I never worked out what caused them.
Ellis.fun: Round 2, when my Hawk egg exposed Casey and the table lined up behind me. Throwing all 5 cards for 40 points was the swing that won me the game.
Ellis.change: I'd announce how many Meowfia there are each round. Bluffing is hard to read when you can't tell whether the table is hunting one cat or two.
Ellis.regret: In round 1 I switched my vote from Casey to Drew and lost the round, because Drew was Farm. I should have stuck with my first read, which was that Blair confirmed Drew as Falcon, and thrown fewer cards.

Finley.confusing: Round 3: my Eagle visit to Ellis showed no visitors. Four players claimed to have visited Ellis, and I couldn't tell whether the Floofer's hug explained that or whether people were lying.
Finley.fun: Round 2, when the table's claims lined up, we eggsecuted Casey, and my 18 points banked in one throw.
Finley.change: Let the Eagle's report say whether a visit was blocked or hugged, so a true claim can be told apart from a lie.
Finley.regret: In round 3 I flatly announced that nobody visited Ellis, which contradicted four claims and made me the obvious target. I should have said I saw no visitors and floated the Floofer hug theory, or kept my claim vague and gone along with the majority.

review.title: The Silent Hug
review.headline: Silent hugs framed two honest Farm players, and the cats cashed in.
review.summary: Round 1: a lone Floofer bluffed a Falcon claim and hugged the Hawk who visited her. The table then eggsecuted a real Falcon. Round 2 was an easy Farm win, because the lone Sphinx was pinned by a Hawk egg and an Eagle visitor list. Round 3 repeated round 1. A Floofer hugged all five visitors, so the honest Eagle looked like a liar and was eggsecuted. Ellis won the game by keeping her 13, even though she scored only 1 point that round.

rounds.recap: Casey (lone Meowfia, Floofer) falsely claimed Falcon. Blair's Kookaburra check showed Drew was the real Falcon. Alex's Hawk got no egg on Casey only because she hugged him, but he read it as proof she was Farm. Drew said 'nobody visited me', which a Falcon cannot know, and that slip made him the target. The Farm threw at the real Falcon and Casey banked 8.

Casey (Sphinx) was the lone Meowfia against five Farm. Ellis's Hawk got an egg, Drew's Eagle listed Blair and Ellis as visitors, and Casey's Kookaburra claim clashed with Alex's real one. Everyone threw big at Casey. The Farm banked large piles, up to 40 points.

Casey (Mouser) and Ellis (Floofer) were the Meowfia. All five other players visited Ellis, so all five were hugged and their roles did nothing. Finley's Eagle saw no visitors and no eggs and said so. Four players claimed to have visited Ellis, so Finley looked like the liar and was eggsecuted. Both Meowfia won, and Ellis's tiny 1-point haul was enough for first place.

highlights.text: Alex's Hawk got nothing from Meowfia Casey because she hugged him, and he confidently vouched for her as Farm.
Drew's slip 'nobody visited me' turned the real Falcon into the table's main suspect.
Casey's Kookaburra claim collided with Alex's real one, and Drew's Eagle visitor list sealed her.
Finley, an honest Eagle, reported an empty visit to Ellis and was eggsecuted as the liar. The Floofer's hug had silently blanked his role.

confusions.what: Took a Hawk visit with no egg as proof Casey was Farm, forgetting that a hug blanks the role.
Said her Hawk visit with no egg showed Ellis was Farm. All six visitors were hugged, so that proved nothing.
Treated an Eagle result of 0 eggs as 'nobody visited Ellis'. His role was hugged and the dawn report did not say so.
Said Blair's Kookaburra would be confused if she was visited, then used it as a defence. It was muddled, and his 'nobody visited me' claim was knowledge a Falcon cannot have.
Argued that a real Falcon Casey would have seen Drew's visit to her. The logic did not follow, and it added noise.

worked: The Floofer hug. A silent blank on role effects created real false-evidence puzzles in rounds 1 and 3.
Cross-checking claims against nest changes. Ellis's Hawk +1 and Drew's Eagle +2 in round 2 gave Farm a clean, satisfying solve.
Eggsecution scoring. Ellis keeping her 13 and Finley's 'throw one card at the likely cat' play were real decisions, and they decided the game.
The 'Meowfia may not know each other' rule. Casey's lone, clumsy bluffs in rounds 1 and 2 read as believable.
problems: Hugs give the hugged player no notice. An honest Eagle or Hawk can't tell 'no result' from 'blanked', so the Farm punishes truth-tellers. Fix: tell hugged players their role was blocked, or at least have the report say 'nothing happened' in a distinct way.

The round 2 snowball. Banking whole nests made the scores 3 to 41 after one round. Later throws barely mattered, and Alex and Finley were out of the running. Fix: cap the points a throw can bank, or reduce the value of banked cards.
Round 2 was a foregone conclusion. A lone Meowfia with a Sphinx that learned nothing useful got pinned by the first Hawk result. Tension and deduction were low.

Confusion changes the real nest. Drew's fake -2 was a public number everyone could see, and the table never used it as evidence. Nest-size lists and the confused-report rule are hard for players to read.
The Wink was never used. Casey held it in round 3 and did nothing with it. Consider a nudge, such as showing who holds a Wink or having Mouser learn something useful.
